top_entities.name: Romania
top_entities.news_summary: More than 1,000 sheep and livestock farmers from across Romania protested outside the government building in Bucharest on 15 September 2026 over the government's handling of a peste des petits ruminants (PPR) outbreak and a resulting halt to live-animal exports. Protesters broke through a security cordon; gendarmerie responded with tear gas. 26 people were detained and 24 injured (including 8 gendarmes). President Nicusor Dan condemned the violence on both sides.

top_entities.name: Chile
top_entities.news_summary: On 11 September 2026 (the anniversary of the 1973 coup), Chilean police clashed with protesters in Santiago as the new far-right government of President Jose Antonio Kast held no official commemoration -- the first time since the 1990 return to democracy. Police used tear gas and water cannons; 284 people were detained nationally, including 31 minors. Earlier in September, thousands of students marched against Kast government budget cuts to education and school meals.

top_entities.name: Boston Dynamics (SPOT demo)
top_entities.news_summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) began a formal procurement process (expected solicitation start 4 September 2026, reported through 9 September) to spend up to $2 million on Boston Dynamics Spot robots for 'inspection, situational awareness, and hazard assessment.' Boston Dynamics said ICE must follow the same usage terms as every customer, including a ban on weaponizing Spot and a public-use-policy requirement for law-enforcement customers.

top_entities.name: United States
top_entities.news_summary: UN human rights chief Volker Turk told the UN Human Rights Council on 7 September 2026 that four more people had died in US immigration (ICE) custody since his last update in June, bringing the 2026 total to 23 deaths, and demanded accountability. He also voiced alarm at ICE's reported plans to equip agents with electric shock gloves, warning it would increase the violence associated with operations.

top_entities.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
top_entities.news_summary: Police fired tear gas and warning shots and arrested activists as hundreds protested in Kinshasa and other DRC cities on 15-16 September 2026 against President Felix Tshisekedi's proposed constitutional changes, which critics say could allow him to seek a third term. Demonstrators clashed with pro-government activists; opposition parties and the Catholic Church condemned the proposal.

top_entities.name: Bolivia
top_entities.news_summary: On 14 September 2026 Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz signed a decree extending the country's state of exception by 90 more days. On 15 September, presidential spokesman Jose Luis Galvez warned the government could declare a full state of siege -- 'we will use constitutional force, and we will use the military' -- if diesel-subsidy-related blockades return. Distinct from the 2026-09-14 cycle's already-assessed central-bank currency-intervention finding.

top_entities.name: Starbucks
top_entities.news_summary: On 4 September 2026 the 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals declined to enforce most of an NLRB ruling that Starbucks illegally threatened employees over unionizing at a Wichita, Kansas store, rejecting claims tied to reduced hours and a closed hiring portal, but upheld the finding that a manager illegally threatened to deny maternity leave benefits to a pregnant employee if the store unionized.

sector_alerts.title: Spain: Ceuta migration-crisis protests predate this window by one day
sector_alerts.summary: Roughly 50,000 people protested in Madrid on 2 September 2026 (with large protests also in Barcelona, Valencia and Seville) over the government's handling of the Ceuta migrant crisis; police used rubber bullets and tear gas after the Madrid demonstration. The core event falls one day before this scan's 3-17 September lookback window and is not used to flag Spain, Valencia, or Seville this cycle -- disclosed here as context only, not a coverage gap. Spain carries a pending change proposal from an earlier cycle.

sector_alerts.title: Interpublic Group: 15,000-job Omnicom merger cut, sourcing undated
sector_alerts.summary: Omnicom CFO Phil Angelastro confirmed at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference (10 September 2026) that combined Omnicom/Interpublic Group headcount will fall from ~120,000 to ~105,000 by end of 2026 (~15,000 roles), reported widely on 14 September 2026 (MediaPost, DecisionMarketing, AdNews, Campaign). The underlying facts are well corroborated across many outlets, but no source found this cycle carries a machine-checkable date in its URL, so this is carried as context rather than a flagged top_entities item per the evidence-date-discipline rule (undated sourcing cannot independently support a priority flag). Recommend the assessor or a future cycle locate a day-dated wire source (Reuters/AP/Bloomberg) to promote this to a flag.

sector_alerts.title: Sudan/South Sudan humanitarian funding gap widens
sector_alerts.summary: OCHA briefed the UN Security Council on 17 September 2026 that Sudan's humanitarian appeal is funded at $1.3B of a $2.7B request (under 50%) after 17 months of war. WFP separately reported a deepening South Sudan hunger crisis (7.8M people food-insecure) linked to conflict, climate shocks and funding cuts. Not used to flag Sudan or South Sudan this cycle -- primary driver is conflict/climate, not new in-window government conduct; carried as a watch item for the assessor.

sector_alerts.title: AI-lab safety-researcher departures (Anthropic, Google DeepMind)
sector_alerts.summary: On 10 September 2026, Anthropic's Joe Benton and Google DeepMind's Josh Engels both departed their AI-safety-evaluation roles for METR, an independent AI-evaluation nonprofit; a separate Anthropic researcher (Jacob Coxon) resigned the same week citing labs 'gambling with our lives.' Context for the AI-labs sector; not attributed as adverse conduct to either named lab this cycle.

sector_alerts.title: Dropped candidate: China 'Ethnic Unity Law' misdating recurs
sector_alerts.summary: A search result again described a 'draft Ethnic Unity Law' as September 2026 news. As established in the 2026-09-15 scan, the law actually passed the NPC on 12 March 2026 and took effect 1 July 2026. Dropped again this cycle, not flagged.

sector_alerts.title: Dropped candidate: Venezuela/Maduro capture is a January 2026 event
sector_alerts.summary: An undated search snippet described 'US forces captured Maduro' in a way that read as current. Verified: the capture occurred 3 January 2026 and the New York arraignment was 5 January 2026 -- five months before this scan's lookback window. Dropped, not flagged, after date verification.

sector_alerts.title: Dropped candidate: Zambia opposition-crackdown killing is an August 2026 event
sector_alerts.summary: A UN News item republished in September described the killing of former minister Mutotwe Kafwaya during a post-election security raid. Verified: the raid and killing occurred 14 August 2026 (confirmed 19 August); the September republication is continuing coverage, not a new in-window event. Dropped, not flagged.
